limitations: SQL scan is literal-pattern based; dynamic SQL, SQL assembled by helpers, and statements inside nested helper closures may be omitted or attributed to the surrounding exported function span.
Function call graph is direct lexical call evidence, not runtime reachability or complete transitive closure.
Foreign-key scanner records REFERENCES clauses; inline REFERENCES and deferred schema declarations need migration-by-migration validation.
Transaction markers do not prove correct atomic scope. Caller-owned transactions, async awaits, serialization queues and withinTransaction options need call-path analysis.
No ownership is inferred from function/table names.
candidateArea labels are name-derived triage only and must not be interpreted as domain/table ownership.
Function body extraction is a lightweight lexical scanner, not a full JavaScript parser; regex literal braces and nested template interpolation are residual edge cases.

SQL call-site ownership is assigned by source-line containment in exported function spans; internal helper/module-scope statements may be unowned or attributed to a containing export. Dynamic SQL expressions remain unresolved.

SQL sites not enclosed by an exported function are assigned to the nearest preceding function declaration as an approximate internal-helper attribution; verify before treating that edge as a call-graph fact.
methodology: Function body spans are parsed from exported function declarations while skipping comments and quoted strings/templates; SQL table operations and direct named function calls are lexical static candidates. Regex literals and nested template interpolation may still affect edge cases. Dynamic SQL and helper-mediated access can be missed. Candidate areas are name-derived only and never establish canonical ownership. A global db.prepare/db.exec call-site scan enumerates literal/dynamic SQL arguments, operation types, referenced table candidates and nearest exported function source span.

crossDomainInvariants.invariant: Payment decision/ledger mutation and Marketplace allocation/settlement consequences must remain atomic and idempotent; Payment remains payment authority.
Refund finalization and Marketplace refund/allocation/settlement effects must not partially commit.

Marketplace checkout coordinates existing Catalog, Inventory reservation, Payment allocation and Fulfillment representations under a single idempotent checkout command; do not turn this orchestrator into duplicate domain authorities.
Seller order status transition coordinates Inventory, Payment/refund and Fulfillment consequences; preserve atomicity and lifecycle idempotency.
Receipt posting must atomically persist receipt state and canonical Inventory movements; inventory mutation remains Inventory authority.
Courier assignment, membership/role scope and fulfillment lifecycle transitions must preserve tenant/location authorization and command idempotency.
Service resource availability, commitment and booking transitions must not oversell time slots; booking feasibility remains separate from commitment/execution.
Supplier Network trust/performance are derived evidence views; procurement source facts remain Procurement-owned and evidence visibility/ownership rules remain enforced.
Identity, membership, contextual roles, sessions and device lifecycle form one tenant authorization boundary; never split enforcement across duplicate authorities.
